title: Changes in Size and Limit to Number of Occupants for HDB Rental Flats
what_it_is: Changes in Size and Limit to Number of Occupants for HDB Rental Flats

sections.label: HDB rental flats history
sections.summary: Public rental housing began with HDB 1-, 2- and 3-room flats; 3-room rentals were sold and closed in 1982, and only 1- and 2-room flats were built from 2007.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Public housing first started with Housing and Development Board (HDB) blocks comprising 1-, 2- and 3-room rental flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Subsequently, as part of the Government's overall move to encourage Singaporeans towards home ownership, HDB sold existing 3-room rental flats to the sitting tenants and closed the 3-room rental register in 1982.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Hence, when HDB resumed the rental building programme in 2007, only 1- and 2-room flats were built.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: More than 90% of households in these public rental flats have four or fewer persons living together.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Larger families who form two separate family nuclei, such as grandparents living with parents and children, and need more space may also apply for two separate rental flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: There are no plans to impose a limit on the number of family members who can live in a rental flat or to impose occupancy standards for such flats.

sections.label: Multi-generational family applicants
sections.summary: This typically applies to multi-generational families, and the speaker does not have the numbers but says the applicants are not many.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, this would typically apply to multi-generational families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I do not have the numbers, but the applicants are not many.

sections.label: HDB and social service engagement
sections.summary: The Housing and Development Board and social service agencies are committed to engage these families to understand and tackle their needs holistically.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The Housing and Development Board and the social service agencies are committed to engage these families to better understand their needs and to resolve and tackle them holistically.
